> **Scope.** This page is the *mechanism*, stripped of narrative: what an
> implementer actually has to build, in the order they have to build it.
> The binding decisions are [ADR-078](../../adr/adr-078-orgpath-attribute-schema-15-facet.qmd)
> (facet decomposition), [ADR-121](../../adr/adr-121-orgpath-projection-subset.qmd)
> (projection subset), and [ADR-127](../../adr/adr-127-orgpath-hybrid-derived-path.qmd)
> (the derived path). The executable canon is
> [`codebook.yaml`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/data/orgpath/codebook.yaml)
> (`schema_version: 2.2.0`).

## Why This Page Exists

The OrgPath corpus is large — a twenty-nine-book narrative, a seven-step
operational guide, a dozen binding ADRs. That volume exists because
OrgPath has to be *justified* to architects, auditors, and program
sponsors before anyone will let it near a directory.

None of that is what you build. What you build is five things, and the
whole of it is a couple hundred lines of code plus one YAML file. This
page is those five things.

## Part 1 — A Codebook: Facet → Slot → Allowed Values

One YAML file is the source of truth. It binds each semantic facet to
exactly one `extensionAttribute` slot and, for enumerated facets, to a
closed list of legal values.

| Slot | Facet | Written to the directory? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `extensionAttribute1` | `region` | ✅ — hierarchy |
| `extensionAttribute2` | `department` | ✅ — hierarchy |
| `extensionAttribute3` | `division` | ✅ — hierarchy |
| `extensionAttribute4` | `role` | ❌ defined, not projected |
| `extensionAttribute5` | `cost_center` | ❌ defined, not projected |
| `extensionAttribute6` | `classification` | ✅ |
| `extensionAttribute7` | `hire_date` | ❌ defined, not projected |
| `extensionAttribute8` | `term_date` | ❌ defined, not projected |
| `extensionAttribute9` | `clearance_level` | ✅ |
| `extensionAttribute10` | `account_type` | ✅ |
| `extensionAttribute11` | `admin_tier` | ✅ — tenant extension (ADR-137) |
| `extensionAttribute12` | `device_type` | ✅ — tenant extension (ADR-137) |
| `extensionAttribute13` | `environment` | ✅ — tenant extension (ADR-137) |
| `extensionAttribute14` | reserved for tenant extension | ❌ |
| `extensionAttribute15` | `org_path` | ✅ — **derived**, never authored |

Ten attributes written per object, out of fifteen slots. The
"defined but not projected" distinction is [ADR-121](../../adr/adr-121-orgpath-projection-subset.qmd):
a facet keeps its HR-source-of-truth semantics without consuming a
scarce, tenant-wide directory slot. Only rules that actually target a
facet justify projecting it.

The facet-by-facet detail — enumerations, descriptions, deprecation
handling — is the [OrgPath Codebook](codebook.qmd) page.

## Part 2 — One Pure Function: Derive the Path

Slots 1, 2, and 3 are the hierarchy, in that order. The derived path is
a pure function of them:

```
path = ""
for facet in [region, department, division]:      # fixed order
    v = values.get(facet)
    if not v or v not in codebook[facet]:         # truncate at the first gap
        break
    path += f"{Label}={v}|"                       # trailing "|" ALWAYS
```

```
{region: NCR, department: IT, division: CyberOps}
    → "Region=NCR|Department=IT|Division=CyberOps|"

{region: NCR, division: CyberOps}     # department missing
    → "Region=NCR|"
```

Two invariants carry all the weight, and both are easy to get wrong:

**The trailing delimiter is on every segment, including the last.** That
is what makes a subtree prefix collision-free — without the terminator, a
prefix targeting the `East` division also captures `Eastern` and
`Easton`, and the rule looks correct in review. The collision table is
worked through on the [Hybrid OrgPath Model](hybrid-orgpath-model.qmd)
page; CI enforces the rule repo-wide
([`check_orgpath_prefix_delimiter.py`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/scripts/check_orgpath_prefix_delimiter.py)).

**Composition truncates at the first unpopulated or invalid facet**, so
the value is always a contiguous hierarchy prefix — never a path with a
hole punched in the middle of it. An out-of-enumeration value is the
*facet's* drift finding; the path simply stops short of it.

The two shipped implementations of this function must agree:

| Surface | Implementation |
| :--- | :--- |
| Python | `Codebook.derive_org_path` in [`src/uiao/modernization/orgtree/codebook.py`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/modernization/orgtree/codebook.py) |
| PowerShell | `New-OrgPath` in [`tools/powershell/UIAO.OrgPath/UIAO.OrgPath.psm1`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/tools/powershell/UIAO.OrgPath/UIAO.OrgPath.psm1) |

## Part 3 — Write All Seven in One Call

The property name differs by object type. This is the single most common
implementation mistake, because the wrong one fails quietly rather than
loudly:

| Plane | Where the values live |
| :--- | :--- |
| Entra user | `Update-MgUser` → `onPremisesExtensionAttributes` |
| Entra device | `Update-MgDevice` → `extensionAttributes` |
| Azure resource | ARM tag named `OrgPath`, carrying the derived string |

Slot 15 is recomputed on every stamp. It is never read back, edited, and
written — that is the dual-authoring failure mode the derivation exists
to foreclose. `Update-OrgAttributes` in the `UIAO.OrgPath` module writes
the governance facets and the derived path together.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The hybrid-sync trap
For users synced from on-premises Active Directory,
`onPremisesExtensionAttributes` is **read-only in the cloud**. The stamp
has to happen on-prem and sync down, or wait until the object is
cloud-only. Discovering this after building a cloud-side writer is a
rewrite, not a patch.
:::

## Part 4 — Query It Two Ways

This is the payoff, and the reason both layers exist. Neither mechanism
can express the other's questions.

*"Privileged, cleared, NCR-based"* is boolean facet composition over the
governance layer:

```
(user.extensionAttribute9 -eq "TopSecret") and (user.extensionAttribute1 -eq "NCR")
```

*"IT/CyberOps and everything beneath it, at any future depth"* is a single
prefix predicate against the inheritance layer:

```
(device.extensionAttribute15 -startsWith "Region=NCR|Department=IT|")
```

The prefix form is what survives a reorganization: a branch rule written
once keeps covering descendants that do not exist yet. The facet form is
what survives a *question* that has nothing to do with hierarchy.

Never build a prefix by string concatenation — `Get-OrgPathPrefix`
normalizes one idempotently, appending the terminator when it is missing.

## Part 5 — Drift Is Recompute-and-Compare

Because the path is a pure function of slots 1–3, divergence is
mechanically detectable rather than a matter of judgment:

- **Derived-path drift** — recompute from the governance facets, compare
  to the stored slot-15 value, flag any mismatch
  (`Test-OrgPathDrift`, and the Python drift engine's derived-path check
  in [`src/uiao/governance/drift_engine.py`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/governance/drift_engine.py)).
- **Value drift** — any facet value absent from its codebook enumeration
  is `DRIFT-SEMANTIC`, independently of the path.

These are separate findings on purpose. A bad `division` value produces
one finding about the facet, not a cascade of confusing findings about
every rule that reads the path.

## The Whole Thing in One Sentence

> Stamp seven validated facet values into fixed `extensionAttribute`
> slots on every directory object, derive slot 15 as
> `Region=…|Department=…|Division=…|` with a mandatory trailing pipe,
> then target policy either by boolean facet predicates or by path
> prefix — and treat any stored path that does not equal the recomputed
> one as drift.

## What This Page Leaves Out

Everything else in the corpus is either a *consumer* of the contract
above or a *transport* for it, and none of it changes the five parts:

| Concern | Where it lives |
| :--- | :--- |
| Facet enumerations and deprecation | [OrgPath Codebook](codebook.qmd) |
| Why two layers, and the collision proof | [Hybrid OrgPath Model](hybrid-orgpath-model.qmd) |
| Running it end-to-end on sample data | [Governance golden path](../../docs/orgpath-golden-path.qmd) |
| Rolling it onto a real tenant | [OrgPath implementation guides](../operational-guides/orgpath-implementation/index.qmd) |
| Non-Microsoft directories and clouds | [Portability model](orgpath-portability.qmd) |
| Dynamic groups, AUs, policy targeting | [Dynamic groups](dynamic-groups.qmd), [delegation](delegation.qmd) |

If you were rebuilding OrgPath from scratch, the codebook YAML plus the
derivation function plus a directory writer is a working implementation.
Everything above that line is governance; everything below it is
plumbing.
